smt-2012-algebra-tiebreaker-01.title: Vieta
smt-2012-algebra-tiebreaker-01.body:
$a+b=4$, $ab=2$. Then $a^2+b^2=16-4=12$ and $a^3+b^3=64-3\cdot2\cdot4=40$. The monic quadratic is $(x-12)(x-40)$; the sum of its coefficients is its value at $x=1$: $(-11)(-39)=429$.

**Answer: 429**

smt-2012-algebra-tiebreaker-03.title: Angle addition
smt-2012-algebra-tiebreaker-03.body:
Multiply by $\cos(60^\circ-\alpha)$ and write $1=2\sin30^\circ$, $\sqrt3=2\cos30^\circ$: the left side becomes $2\sin(30^\circ+60^\circ-\alpha)=2\cos\alpha$. So $\dfrac{\cos(60^\circ-\alpha)}{\sin\alpha}=2\cos\alpha$, i.e. $\cos(60^\circ-\alpha)=\sin2\alpha$, i.e. $\sin(\alpha+30^\circ)=\sin2\alpha$.

Either $2\alpha=\alpha+30^\circ$ giving $\alpha=30^\circ$, or $2\alpha+\alpha+30^\circ=180^\circ$ giving $\alpha=50^\circ$. Both lie in $(0^\circ,90^\circ)$ and satisfy the original equation (checked numerically).

**Answer: $30^\circ$ and $50^\circ$**
